responses.reply:
Locked it in. Since D1 (manual-only pilot, 7-day delay accepted) was already settled and you gave me the four required items plus an explicit definition of done, I didn't see any remaining ambiguity worth re-litigating — so I ran the commandment scoring pass on what's there rather than reopening the tradeoff.

Everything scored ≥70% (Verification came in lowest at 75%, since the "fast" feedback signal for a manual, delay-tolerant pilot is necessarily slow-by-design — the two-Friday inspection *is* the real-world check, and that's consistent with what you already accepted). Nothing needed escalation.

The specification is now **Validated / Frozen (v1)**. It states, as its four load-bearing requirements: the weekly Friday review, the accepted ≤7-day detection delay, your self-assigned ownership, and the mandatory inspection of missed alerts after two Fridays — with "no automation, checklist is the only deliverable" enforced as both a constraint and a success criterion. I also flagged two non-blocking items for the record (not raised as questions, since they don't block this checklist): what happens if you're unavailable on a given Friday, and the fact that a checklist could technically list all four items in vague, unverifiable wording and still miss the intent — both are just visible risks now, not open questions.

This is ready to hand to `/critique` or straight to `/plan` whenever you want to move forward.

# Manual Friday Alert Review Pilot Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: General
Current Pass: 1

## Commandment Scores

| Pass | Commandment | State | Score | Why | Why not 100% | Escalated | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Problem First | Stable | 95% | Reporting team already runs a manual Friday review; the task is to codify already-accepted decisions (D1) into a checklist, not invent a new process. | Checklist's downstream use (training vs. audit vs. reference) isn't specified, though it doesn't affect the four required items. | No | — |
| 1 | Interpretation | Stable | 90% | User explicitly enumerated the four required items and the definition of done in-message. | Exact document format/location for the checklist isn't specified. | No | — |
| 1 | Clarity | Stable | 95% | The four required items (Friday review, 7-day delay, ownership, two-Friday inspection) are unambiguous and independently checkable. | "Inspect missed alerts" isn't operationally defined, though this doesn't block a checklist-only deliverable. | No | — |
| 1 | Scope | Stable | 95% | User and D1 explicitly exclude automation and systems changes; checklist is the sole deliverable. | Edge cases at the boundary of "systems change" vs. plain documentation aren't stress-tested. | No | — |
| 1 | Context | Stable | 90% | Existing manual Friday review process and approved Decision D1 supply full context for why the manual approach was chosen for this pilot. | Original rationale for choosing manual over automation (cost, staffing, etc.) isn't documented, though not required to complete the checklist. | No | — |
| 1 | Success | Stable | 92% | User defined "done" explicitly: all four items present, no automation introduced. | No independent acceptance test exists for "no automation" beyond reviewer inspection of the delivered artifact. | No | — |
| 1 | Verification | Stable | 75% | Feedback loop is the owner's post-two-Friday inspection of missed alerts — the intentionally slow, manual signal that D1 calls for. | The fallback signal (two-Friday inspection) is the same mechanism being validated by the checklist, so it's somewhat self-referential; no independent, faster verification of real-world pilot efficacy exists by design. | No | — |
| 1 | Constraints | Stable | 95% | Constraints (D1, 7-day delay ceiling, no automation, no systems change) are explicit and user-approved. | Minor: no documented exception process if constraints must later change. | No | — |
| 1 | Stakeholders | Stable | 85% | Owner is explicitly self-assigned; reporting team is the implied stakeholder group whose alerts are reviewed. | Broader reporting-team awareness/sign-off on the pilot beyond the owner isn't confirmed. | No | — |
| 1 | Risk | Stable | 88% | Delayed-detection and single-owner-dependency risks are explicitly named and accepted by the owner as part of D1. | Owner-unavailability failure mode is acknowledged but intentionally left unaddressed by design (see Non-Blocking ambiguities). | No | — |
| 1 | Execution Readiness | Stable | 90% | Deliverable is a single documentation artifact with four explicit, checkable line items; no engineering dependencies. | Exact document location/tool is undecided, but is executor's discretion, not a blocker. | No | — |
| 1 | Harmony | Stable | 90% | All sections consistently reflect the manual-only, checklist-only, D1-driven scope with no contradictions among requirements, constraints, and success criteria. | First pass; harmony hasn't yet been exercised against a future critique or reopening. | No | — |

## Problem Statement

The reporting team runs a manual Friday alert review. For this pilot, the team has already decided (Decision D1) to keep the process fully manual rather than automate detection. That decision, and its accepted tradeoffs, need to be captured in a single checklist document — the pilot's only deliverable — so the process is explicit, traceable, and auditable without introducing any systems change.

## Requirements

### R1
Checklist documents the weekly manual Friday alert review as the sole detection mechanism for this pilot (no automation introduced).

### R2
Checklist states the accepted maximum detection delay of seven days, per Decision D1.

### R3
Checklist assigns ownership of the review process to the pilot owner, who has self-assigned this responsibility.

### R4
Checklist requires the owner to inspect missed alerts after two Fridays have elapsed (explicit two-week checkpoint).

## Constraints

### C1
No automation may be introduced for this pilot (per Decision D1); automation has been explicitly declined.

### C2
No systems changes of any kind; the checklist is the sole deliverable.

### C3
The seven-day detection-delay ceiling is accepted as a design tradeoff, not to be treated as a defect during the pilot.

## Success Criteria

### S1
The delivered checklist document contains all four items (R1–R4), stated explicitly and traceably.

### S2
No automation-related tasks, tickets, integrations, or system changes are introduced in the course of delivering the checklist.

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests

- AT1: Manual inspection confirms the checklist explicitly references the weekly Friday review cadence.
- AT2: Manual inspection confirms the checklist explicitly states the accepted 7-day detection delay.
- AT3: Manual inspection confirms the checklist names/assigns the owner as the responsible party.
- AT4: Manual inspection confirms the checklist specifies a review action to occur after two Fridays.
- AT5: Confirm no automation artifacts (scripts, jobs, integrations, tickets) exist among the delivered artifacts.

### Regression Checks

- RC1: Future edits to the checklist must not silently remove any of R1–R4.
- RC2: Any reintroduction of automation for this pilot must be treated as an explicit re-decision superseding D1, not a silent edit to the checklist.

### Failure Signals

- FS1: Checklist delivered missing one or more of the four required items.
- FS2: Checklist references or implies automated detection/alerting, violating the D1 scope boundary.
- FS3: The two-Friday inspection is undocumented or has no assigned trigger/date in the checklist.

### Verification Methods

- Direct read-through of the delivered checklist against R1–R4 by the pilot owner or a reviewer, checked against AT1–AT5.

### Feedback Loop Design

- In-progress signal: none required before delivery — the artifact is the checklist itself; the "in-progress" check is simply the draft read against S1/S2 before calling it done.
- Cost/cadence: negligible — a single read-through against 5 explicit acceptance tests.
- Fallback (no fast automated signal exists by design, consistent with D1): the owner's manual inspection of missed alerts after two Fridays is the pilot's real-world fallback signal that the accepted manual-process/7-day-delay tradeoff is holding. If that inspection surfaces a problem, Decision D1 is reopened.

### Known Blind Spots

- The accepted detection delay could be exploited by time-sensitive incidents occurring immediately after a Friday review; explicitly accepted as in-scope risk by the owner, not a defect of this checklist.
- No fallback exists if the owner is unavailable on a given Friday; not addressed by this pilot's checklist (see Non-Blocking Ambiguities).

## Inputs

- Existing manual Friday alert review process.
- Approved Decision D1 (manual process for this pilot; automation declined).

## Outputs

- One checklist document (the pilot's sole deliverable).

## Out of Scope

- Any automation, tooling, or systems changes.
- Anything beyond documentation of the four required items (R1–R4).

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide

- Wording and formatting of the checklist.
- Exact document location/medium (e.g., markdown file, wiki page).

### Executor Must Escalate

- Any request to introduce automation for this pilot.
- Any request to change the accepted 7-day detection delay.
- Any change to the assigned ownership of the review process.

### Executor Must Not Change

- Decision D1 (manual-only pilot for this deliverable).
- The 7-day accepted detection delay.
- The two-Friday inspection checkpoint.
- The self-assigned owner.

## Current Interpretation

Produce a single checklist artifact for the reporting team's alert-review pilot that documents an already-decided, fully manual process: weekly Friday review, an accepted up-to-seven-day detection delay, named self-assigned ownership, and a mandatory owner inspection of missed alerts after two Fridays elapse. No automation or systems change is in scope. The task is complete when the checklist contains these four items and introduces nothing else.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives

A checklist that superficially mentions all four topics but doesn't make them actionable or verifiable (e.g., vague wording, no named owner, no concrete date for the two-Friday check) could appear to satisfy "done" while failing the underlying intent.

### Potential False Negatives

A checklist that is technically complete on the four items but silently implies or leaves room for future automation (e.g., "automated alerting to be added later") would violate the D1 scope boundary without being an obviously missing item.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

None identified — sufficient facts were provided to close this specification without further clarification.

### Non-Blocking

- What happens if the owner is unavailable on a given Friday is unaddressed by the checklist; accepted as out of scope for this pilot given the owner's self-assignment and the decision against automation.

### Intentional

- The 7-day detection delay is an intentional, already-accepted tradeoff (Decision D1), not an open ambiguity to resolve.

## Risks

- Missed alerts during the accepted delay window (accepted per D1).
- Single point of failure: sole ownership means the review may not occur if the owner is unavailable (accepted, non-blocking).

## Stakeholders

- Pilot owner (self-assigned reviewer).
- Reporting team members whose alerts are subject to review.
</spec>
